inspiration: repipe round 11 need finite-field-squaring-loop; the second inlined GF(2^8) multiply emitted `v6 = 0; v3 = a0; while (a0 = v6, v7 = a0 != 0, v7)`, skipping the squaring loop for every input

gates.make rust-test: green; 379 `test result` lines, all `0 failed`, no panics (run with `env -u KUNA_DECOMP_TEST` so the verify_w10_* oracle tests do not point at this build)

promoted_probe.why: CI has no dataset. covertrim_x86_64 is a 4944-byte project-authored ELF carrying the same instruction shape (GF(2^8) inverse, two inlined multiplies, the R9B -> CL -> R11B copy cycle across the outer back edge). Measured: the unpatched tree emits the identical `v6 = 0; v3 = a0; while (a0 = v6, v7 = a0 != 0, v7)` on it. A gcc -O2 build of the same C source does NOT reproduce it -- gcc allocates around the cycle -- so the fixture is hand-written assembly.
promoted_probe.strengthened: the filed acceptance is absence-only and is satisfiable by reordering two lines, so the promoted probe also pins the positive witness the round-9 refuter asked for: TWO distinct iterators, each initialised from the input and each shifted (`(v[0-9]+) = a0; ... \1 >>= 1; ... (v[0-9]+) = a0; ... \2 >>= 1;`). Measured on the fixture: unpatched fails BOTH clauses, patched passes both.

sweep.method: kuna decompile-all, unpatched build vs patched build, over 41 decbench images sampled every 20th across O0 / O2 / O2-noinline
sweep.note: the mechanism can only REFUSE a merge, never accept one, so every hunk is a HighVariable split: a value that shared a name now has its own, and the copy that was implicit becomes explicit. Three changed hunks were read against the disassembly.
inspected: zlib/minigzip `scan_tree`: `v9` splits into `v14`/`v9`/`v10`; the shift-and-shadow loop is line-for-line equivalent

libedit `history_truncate_file` @0x2e2dc (O0, stack-slot pointer): the unpatched output DROPPED an instruction. `addq $0x1,-0x1058(%rbp)` at 0x2e2a7 had no rendering at all, because the merged high forced an eager `cp = v2` writeback that destroyed the one-step-behind shadow carrying the +1. Patched emits `v2 = cp;` there, and `if (v5 <= cp)` now compares the incremented pointer, matching `cmp %rax,-0x1058(%rbp)` at 0x2e2bc.

coreutils/sort `init_node`: the unpatched output merged the incoming `parent` parameter with `node_pool` and emitted the self-referential `parent = node_pool; ... parent->parent = (merge_node *)parent; ... parent->level = parent->level + 1`. Patched keeps them apart (`parent_00 = node_pool; parent_00->parent = (merge_node *)parent; parent_00->level = parent->level + 1`) and, with the cover no longer fragmented, folds four address temporaries (`v1 = &parent->nlo; v5 = *v1 >> 1;`) back into direct field reads.

speed_method: warmup + median of 5, `kuna decompile-all` per image, unpatched main-tree release binary vs patched worktree release binary, KUNA_DECOMP_DBG unset so each driver forks its own engine
speed_target: decompile-all over 4 images (O2 sort, O2 dpkg, O0 libedit, O2 minigzip)
speed_note: per-image medians: sort -1.00%, dpkg +1.63%, libedit +0.56%, minigzip -4.44%. Two of four are negative, so the spread is noise, not cost -- consistent with the mechanism (one extra dirty-bit write on a path that already reallocates a Cover). docs/features/returncopysplit/record.json measured a -20.23%/-12.18% noise floor on byte-identical output on this box, so nothing under 20% is a measurement.
decisions: The filed hypothesis ('possibly incorrect merging or placement of loop-carried copies') is UPHELD, and the round-9 refuter's sharpening is confirmed exactly: the copy cycle R9B -> CL -> R11B across the outer back edge is the trigger, and the parameter's HighVariable is NOT an attractor.

The cause is one level below the merge logic, and it is a port loss rather than a design choice. C++ `Varnode::calcCover` sets `coverdirty` through `setFlags`, which forwards the bit to `high->coverDirty()` (varnode.cc:371-380). kuna's arena model cannot reach `high_bank` from `Varnode::set_flags`, and `docs/rust-port/losses.md` records the notification as reconciled at the Funcdata level -- but only one call site actually reconciled it. `Funcdata::set_varnode_properties`, which re-allocates a Cover the preceding `op_unset_output` dropped, did not.

Measured, not argued. `Merge::merge` was instrumented to dump both HighVariables' per-instance Covers at every intersection test. At the merge that creates the defect, `unique:10000054` -- a copy trim `Merge::merge_op` inserted, already a member of CL's high -- carries `cov=` (empty), while the SAME varnode carries `b2:0-0;b12:2200002-ffffffff;b13:0-ffffffff;b14:0-800002;b18:0-ffffffff;` one merge later. `Cover::intersect` scores an empty block 0, so the member is treated as live nowhere and the overlapping merge is accepted.

No option, and this is deliberate. The rule gates behaviour that is a judgement call; a HighVariable holding two values that are live at the same instant is not one. The mechanism is also one-directional: restoring the dirty bit can only make an intersection test see MORE cover, so merges can only be refused, never accepted. It cannot delete or move a statement -- and the sweep found the opposite, that the unpatched build was the one dropping one (libedit above).

Scoped to the re-allocation path only. `Varnode::set_def`, `add_descend` and `erase_descend` also set the bit without forwarding it; those are far hotter and would dirty many more highs per pass. They are a separate change with separate evidence and are not touched here.

No existing option covers it: the round-9 refuter measured paramcopyhoist, condexeplace, foldcallret, simdlane, tiedstorekeep, calleepop and `--mode reliable` all leaving the defect at 50 lines, and the catalog's single merge-aggressiveness row (paramcopyhoist) is inert on this function.
